summary: tighten migration sudoers — path-pin -f or move to guru_migrator role
description:
Current sudoers entry on guru-web-prod:
  deploy ALL=(postgres) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1

This lets the deploy user run arbitrary SQL as postgres on the guru DB. Postgres is a superuser, so blast radius is full DDL/DML on every schema (app + corpus). The pattern is no-restriction-by-design — deploy can pipe any SQL via stdin.

Two ways to tighten, in order of effort:

1. Path-pinned -f. Change deploy.sh to write each migration body (with SET ROLE prefix) to a temp file under $RELEASE/migrations/, then 'psql … -f <file>'. Sudoers becomes:
     deploy ALL=(postgres) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/psql -d guru -1 -f /srv/guru-web/releases/*/migrations/*.sql
   Modest win — deploy can still write any file but only execute SQL inside an approved git checkout.

2. Separate migrator role (real win). vps-bootstrap.sh creates a guru_migrator postgres role with DDL grants on app tables only (users, sessions, queries, user_preferences, quota, rate_limits) — never corpus.*. deploy.sh runs migrations as guru_migrator, never postgres-the-superuser. Limits damage if deploy is compromised.

Done when:
- Approach decided (review + small ADR or PR description)
- vps-bootstrap.sh + deploy.sh + /etc/sudoers.d/deploy updated to match
- Existing VPS hand-patch documented in deploy/README.md (same pattern as recent deploy.sh fixes)

resolution.note: Migrations now run as the guru DB owner via peer auth on the guru OS user. Sudoers stanza tightened to (guru) target. One-time hand-patch of /etc/sudoers.d/deploy on existing VPSes documented in README.
